title: Aurora to pay $23M for two Lower Arkansas Valley farms
h1: Aurora City Council approved $23 million to buy land and water from two century-old family farms in the Lower Arkansas Valley
description: Aurora City Council voted unanimously on November 23, 2026 to pay $23 million for two Lower Arkansas Valley farms and 1,360 Catlin Canal water shares.
standfirst: The Hirakata and Hanagan families will lease their land back and keep farming. Aurora may take the water in three years out of every 10.
keywords: Aurora Water farm purchase, Lower Arkansas Valley water, Catlin Canal shares, Hirakata farm Rocky Ford, Hanagan farm La Junta, buy and dry Colorado
takeaways: The council vote on November 23, 2026 was unanimous and covers two contracts of $11.5 million each.
Aurora gets 1,396 acres and 1,360 shares of the Catlin Canal across the two farms.
The families can lease the land back for 10 years, with extensions for another 20.
body: Aurora City Council voted unanimously on Monday, November 23, 2026, to spend $23 million on land and water from two century-old family farms in the Lower Arkansas Valley, The Colorado Sun reported.

There are two contracts of $11.5 million each, according to the Sun. One buys 667 acres at Rocky Ford from the Hirakata family, along with 654 shares of the Catlin Canal, which carries Arkansas River water to farms. The other buys 729 acres near La Junta from the Hanagan family farm, with 706 canal shares.

One share can deliver one to two acre-feet of water a year, depending on the weather. An acre-foot covers the needs of two to three urban households for a year, the Sun reported. The money comes from Aurora Water's capital water fund.

Both families have a 10-year deal to lease the land back and keep farming, with extensions available for another 20 years. Aurora has agreed to take the water for city use in only three years out of any 10-year period.

The city has used that limit before. In 2024 it moved to buy a 4,806-acre Otero County property on the same canal for $80 million, with withdrawals capped at three times in any 10 years, Sentinel Colorado reported at the time. Aurora has bought water in the valley since the 1970s, the Sentinel reported, including deals in which farmland was dried up.

The Lower Arkansas Valley Water Conservancy District wants cities to take a portion of a farm's water every year instead of all of it in some years. That approach "is much more farmer-friendly," the district's general manager, Jack Goble, told the Sun. He said it lets farmers work idle ground into their crop rotations and plan with more certainty.

Aurora Water supply chief Alex Davis told the Sun that taking 30% each year could require state legislation. Utility officials said it would also need renegotiated agreements with Lower Arkansas Valley interests and approval from state water courts.
The council vote approves the two contracts. Any move to yearly partial transfers depends on those new agreements and court approvals, so the three-in-10-year terms apply for now.

faq.q: How much is Aurora paying for the Lower Arkansas Valley farms?
faq.a: $23 million in total: $11.5 million each to the Hirakata family at Rocky Ford and the Hanagan family farm near La Junta, The Colorado Sun reported.

faq.q: Will the farms stop growing crops?
faq.a: The families will lease the land back for 10 years, with extensions for another 20, and Aurora has agreed to take the water in only three years out of any 10.
